chain.title: 2020 Design and Construction Standards (adopted by EMC 11-7-25)

min_lane_width_ft.note: Measured from edge of pavement, excluding the gutter/pan — a measurement definition no other corpus jurisdiction gives; City staff may require greater (TC-1 T10).

sign_spacing.note: Work Zone Sign Spacing (X); table gives minimum spacing — increase as needed (T08).
Identical to Aurora across the full range; the 30/35 breakpoint is the municipal pattern (CDOT draws it at 40/45 — both lawful, Table 6B-1 delegates it).

device_spacing.rule: Flat 25 ft taper / 50 ft tangent at EVERY speed (MUTCD: 1.0xS taper / 2.0xS tangent — agree at 25 mph, Englewood stricter above it; 1.8x MUTCD tangent device count at 45 mph). Published device-count formula: min devices = (length / spacing) + 1. The single most quote-relevant delta in the suburb pass.

taper.rule: L = W(S²)/60 at <=40 mph, L = WS at >=45 mph — MUTCD's own formulas, tabulated (105/115/125 @25 ... 270/295/320 @40). No delta.

buffer.rule: Buffer space MAY be placed in advance; recommended for high speed, high volume, or limited sight distance; may be required by City staff based on engineering judgement (T11). Published table matches MUTCD stopping-sight-distance values (155@25 / 200@30 / 250@35 / 305@40 / 360@45).

other.rule: Local entrances: device spacing 10 ft (typ.) within '40-ft limits of reduced spacing' each side of the entrance — roughly nine devices where the general rule would place two or three; every local entrance along the zone carries this cost.
Bike lane taper L = 10 x A (A = bike lane width) — no MUTCD analogue; optional downstream taper 100 ft max; optional parking lane taper 20-50 ft.
Termination: 50 ft (<=30 mph) / 100 ft (>=35 mph) from work area to end of the channelizing device run (TC-2, TC-4); 500 ft from device-run end to the downstream END ROAD WORK sign (TC-4).

geometry.note: TC-1 is the single source of truth for lengths and spacing — every other sheet defers to it explicitly.

deltas.rule: Arrow boards are required for lane closures on arterial and collector city streets (T09).
deltas.baseline: arrow board optional per MUTCD for most single-lane closures

deltas.rule: When work zone operations impact a parking lane, no-parking signs shall be installed a minimum of 24 hours prior to beginning work (T15).
Excavations left open overnight require flashing barricades, unless the Engineer authorizes otherwise in writing.

trigger.condition: excavation left open overnight (only where the Engineer authorizes an exception to the overnight prohibition)

conflict.label: overnight excavations
conflict.rendered: Prohibited (ROW Guide); flashing barricades required where the Engineer authorizes an exception

sources.value: All work properly backfilled prior to end of workday; no open holes or plates overnight
When excavations must remain open overnight: properly marked, flashing barricades unless the Engineer authorizes otherwise in writing

conflict.verdict: Render the prohibition; the flashing-barricade rule applies only under a written Engineer exception (Q-ENG-3).

deltas.rule: Pedestrians shall not be directed across a road with more than 2 lanes without an existing marked crosswalk (TC-5B note 2, verbatim incl. drafting typo in the original) — a hard feasibility gate on ped detours.

trigger.condition: pedestrian detour routed across >2 lanes without an existing marked crosswalk

deltas.rule: At least one lane of traffic in each direction shall be open to public traffic at all times; all lane closures approved by the Engineer prior to closure. Contractor shall not have construction equipment or materials in lanes open to traffic at any time.
A Traffic Control Plan is required for each phase of the work; major changes to the approved TTCP reviewed by the City prior to implementation (T03).

source.doc: Englewood ROW Permit checklist + TC-1 T03

windows.note: Statutory peak ban (law): no construction obstructing arterial/collector traffic.
Outer envelope: no work 7 p.m.-7 a.m. (noise, EMC 6-2-5(E); TC-1 T17).
ROW work default window unless the Traffic Engineer approves otherwise.
Lane closures on arterials and major collectors; all lanes re-opened by 3 pm (T06).

hours.override_note: No work on any City-recognized holiday without prior permission from the Director of Public Works or designee; Public Works must be notified of any Saturday work. The four hours statements mostly NEST: statutory peak ban outermost, 8:30-3:30 general window, 9-3 arterial lane-closure window innermost.

conflict.label: arterial lane-closure reopen time

sources.doc: TC-1 note T06 (2020, adopted by EMC 11-7-25)
sources.value: 9 a.m.–3 p.m., all lanes re-opened by 3 p.m.

conflict.verdict: Rendering the 3:00 p.m. reopen per TC-1 (conservative); the statute alone would allow until 3:30 (Q-ENG-9, narrowed to this half hour).

personnel.rule: 'The Traffic Control Supervisor (TCS) shall be present on site (or be available) at all times during the duration of the project' (TC-1 T04).

conflict.label: TCS: required or encouraged
conflict.rendered: Required (TC-1 T04 carries the weight of law via EMC 11-7-25)

sources.doc: TC-1 T04 (2020 drawings, adopted by EMC 11-7-25)
sources.value: TCS shall be present on site (or be available) at all times
trained individuals 'should' be assigned; City 'strongly encourages' ATSSA training

conflict.verdict: Precedence leans hard toward REQUIRED: TC-1 sits inside a document adopted into the municipal code; the softer wording is guidance beneath it. Open: what '(or be available)' means (Q-ENG-8).

personnel.rule: Flag persons 'when necessary for public safety'; the City may require them (EMC 11-7-14(C)). Flaggers at BOTH ends of the one-lane two-way closure, drawn as required on TC-3.

devices.rule: Devices supplied by the Permittee; at night: reflectorized AND illuminated, or barricade warning lights. Oil flares and kerosene lanterns prohibited as illumination.
Non-applicable construction signs set so traffic cannot see them during non-construction periods, per CDOT Spec 630; devices no longer appropriate removed or covered on work suspension.

hazards.rule: $500/day administrative penalty explicitly covers 'failure to remove temporary construction signage or traffic control devices' — the first corpus penalty aimed squarely at the barricade company's own scope (law adds a 'materially impacts' qualifier the fee schedule omits; both preserved).

source.doc: Englewood 2026 Rate and Fee Schedule + EMC 11-7-23(E)

hazards.rule: Device-maintenance failure: if the contractor is unavailable, the City corrects and the contractor pays actual costs + 50% penalty (EMC 11-7-14(G)).

notes.rule: Unlawful to perform any work in the ROW without a City contractors license (EMC 11-7-4 — the strongest licensing language in the corpus). Excavation permits: Class A, B or D licensed contractor; concrete: D06. Subcontracting expressly allowed; Permittee remains responsible.

Performance bond = total cost of construction (labor + materials) or $5,000, whichever is greater; in force >=2 years after completion and acceptance; City may waive for in-state financial stability. COI naming the City as additional insured AND certificate holder.

Permit expires in 180 days or less; scope growth requires an amended permit BEFORE exceeding scope ($190 amendment fee, which also covers prompt re-application after denial). Work must start within 10 business days of issuance or the permit is invalid; all permit fees non-refundable. Work after expiry or without permit: 2x the calculated fee.

source.doc: EMC 11-7-4 + ROW Permits Guide + 2026 Rate and Fee Schedule

notes.rule: All costs of developing, implementing, and maintaining the TCP are the Permittee's responsibility (EMC 11-7-14(I) — first jurisdiction to state TCP cost allocation in law).
Fee-responds-to-design ambiguity preserved (Q-ENG-2): whether the Nth-lane rate applies only to that lane or replaces the rate for all closed lanes is unresolved.

multi_agency.rule: Work within the US 285, Belleview Ave. and S. Federal Blvd. rights-of-way requires a CDOT permit (the contractor obtains it) and in most cases an Englewood permit; CDOT's M&S standards apply to work zones impacting state highways (T16). On Englewood city streets, Englewood's own TC standards govern — the city does NOT inherit the CDOT 28"/36" cone rule on city work.

source.doc: Englewood Traffic Control Details TC-1 T16 + ROW Permits Guide

items.label: 6th lane closure
items.note: Escalation x2, x2, x1.5, x1.5, x1.5 across lanes 1-6 — superlinear.

items.label: Detour fee, entire road closure
items.note: Applied per LF per day IN ADDITION to lane closure fees; waived for Xcel Category 1/2 emergency gas repairs completed within 3 days.

items.label: Excavation Permit
items.note: Minimum, plus hourly rate; Concrete Permit same.

items.label: Permit Amendment Application Fee
items.note: Covers scope/duration expansion, permittee transfer, prompt re-application after denial, other.

fees.note: The lane-closure ladder is the corpus's most encodable fee-responds-to-design instance: the engine already knows lane count, lane type, closure length, and duration — every input this table needs.

meters.note: Administrative penalties (EMC 11-7-23(E)): working without a valid permit, unlicensed contractor, and failure to timely remove temporary construction signage or TC devices upon completion of work that materially impacts travel.

source.doc: Englewood 2026 Rate and Fee Schedule + EMC 11-7-23(E)

leads.label: Permit review
leads.note: 3-5 business days for all applications; Engineering Division reviews.

leads.label: Inspection notice
leads.note: Call 303-762-2500; inspection window daily 8 AM-3 PM.

leads.label: Lane/alley closure exact dates to Public Works
leads.note: TC-1 T05: at least 24 hours prior.

notices.rule: Notify for any road closure or parking restriction impacting adjacent properties: description of work, times and duration, company name, emergency contact number. Street closures: notices to affected properties >=48 hours before (EMC 11-7-14(B)); coordinate with police, fire, ambulance, other governmental entities, and transit.
Contractor must give notice to all local residents and businesses prior to alley closure (TC-9/TC-10).
